final_answer: Build the read-only audit subprocess pool as a self-contained, additively-isolated section inside lib/parallel.ps1 that never touches the existing worktree/merge/coder path. The pool keeps a script-scoped registry keyed by the captured root PID; each job is launched with Start-Process -PassThru and its returned System.Diagnostics.Process handle is cached alongside the PID, a pidTicks anti-reuse stamp, and a jobId. Liveness is read from the cached object's .HasExited (never Get-Process -Id, which throws on a dead PID and is vulnerable to PID reuse). Each job gets four per-job temp files (roaudit_<guid>.{in,out,err,result}) under Get-ParallelJobsDir, with stdin/stdout/stderr redirected to the three distinct file targets and 'result' written by the job. Start-ReadOnlyAuditJob is fault-tolerant: each Start-Process is wrapped in try/catch and a failed spawn is recorded with proc=$null instead of aborting the launch loop. Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus is non-destructive — it computes the active count by filtering on cached .HasExited and MARKS completed entries inactive (it does not prune/remove them), so the launched 'total' and the proc=$null failure records survive; it returns a structured @{active; total; activePids} object rather than a bare integer. The test tools/test-readonly-parallel.ps1 launches at least 3 'powershell -NoProfile -Command Start-Sleep' jobs (6–8s), repeatedly samples status to PEAK-track the active count, asserts the peak is >=3, and runs [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile on both lib/parallel.ps1 and itself. All eight atoms are adopted (atom-05 in modified, non-destructive form); the work lands as a single atomic commit.

decisions.decision: Add the read-only audit pool as a top-and-tail delimited section inside lib/parallel.ps1 with dedicated function prefixes (Start-ReadOnlyAuditJob, Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus) and zero calls into worktree/merge/cleanup functions.
decisions.rationale: Tri-source consensus (judge 0.90). A clearly marked section with prefixed functions and no calls into New-Worktree/Merge-Worktree/Remove-Worktree/cleanup machinery structurally guarantees read-only audit jobs can never trigger destructive worktree operations. Housing it in lib/parallel.ps1 rather than a new file is justified by shared reuse of Get-ParallelJobsDir.
alternatives_considered: Place the pool in a separate .ps1 file for hard isolation (rejected: it would duplicate Get-ParallelJobsDir; delimited section + prefixes already give isolation)
decisions.test: Static analysis: confirm the new functions sit inside the marked section and grep shows no calls to New-Worktree/Merge-Worktree/Remove-Worktree/Get-WorkerWorktree/Cleanup-WorkerWorktree/Spawn-Worker from the new code.

decisions.decision: Maintain a script-scoped registry ($script:ReadOnlyAuditRegistry) of root-PID job records, each holding jobId, pid, pidTicks (start-time ticks), and the cached System.Diagnostics.Process handle.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (judge 0.8475). A registry keyed by root PID with a cached handle plus pidTicks is the backbone: pidTicks defends against PID reuse and the cached handle powers the atom-03 liveness check. A 'synchronized' hashtable is unnecessary because Start-Process spawns external OS processes, not in-runspace threads, so a plain script-scoped hashtable suffices.
alternatives_considered: Synchronized/thread-safe hashtable (rejected: no in-runspace concurrency to guard against; adds needless overhead)
Store only bare PIDs without cached handle (rejected: forces Get-Process -Id liveness, which throws and races on PID reuse)
decisions.test: After launching jobs, inspect $script:ReadOnlyAuditRegistry and confirm it is script-scoped and each entry contains jobId, pid, pidTicks, and a cached System.Diagnostics.Process handle.

decisions.decision: Capture the root PID via Start-Process -PassThru, cache the returned Process object in the registry, and derive job liveness from that object's .HasExited property.
decisions.rationale: Consensus and canonically correct PowerShell (judge 0.9225, highest of the set). Reading .HasExited on the owned handle avoids both the PID-reuse race and the throw-on-missing behavior of Get-Process -Id; because the session owns these processes there is no access-denied edge case.
alternatives_considered: Get-Process -Id <pid> for liveness (rejected: throws when the process has exited and can misidentify a reused PID as alive)
decisions.test: Confirm Start-ReadOnlyAuditJob uses Start-Process -PassThru and Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus checks the cached object's .HasExited rather than querying Get-Process -Id.

decisions.decision: Allocate four per-job temp files (input, output, error, result) under Get-ParallelJobsDir with a roaudit_<guid> prefix, redirecting stdin/stdout/stderr to the three distinct file targets via Start-Process -RedirectStandard*.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (judge 0.834). Four files under Get-ParallelJobsDir matches the existing parallel-jobs convention; the roaudit_ prefix prevents collisions with worker jobs. Only three are redirect targets (distinct files avoid the same-file redirect error) while 'result' is written by the job itself.
alternatives_considered: Fewer/shared files or reusing one file for multiple streams (rejected: collision risk across jobs and Start-Process errors when the same file backs more than one redirect)
decisions.test: During a job run, verify roaudit_<guid>.{in,out,err,result} are created under Get-ParallelJobsDir and Start-Process redirects stdin/stdout/stderr to the in/out/err files.

decisions.decision: Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus computes the active count by filtering on each cached handle's .HasExited and MARKS completed entries inactive WITHOUT removing them; any real cleanup of stale entries/temp files lives in a separate maintenance function. (atom-05 modified per judge.)
decisions.rationale: Single-source (A), modified by judge (0.68). The intent — never count dead processes as active — is correct, but destructive pruning inside a Get- (read) verb mutates state, discards the metadata/result-file pointers needed afterward, and breaks the launched 'total' count (atom-06) and the proc=$null failed-job records (atom-08). Marking-not-removing preserves all of that while still excluding dead jobs from 'active'.
alternatives_considered: Destructively prune completed/missing processes from the registry inside the getter (rejected — see rejected[])
Leave dead entries counted and prune elsewhere only (rejected: would over-report active)
decisions.test: Launch several jobs, let some finish, call Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus: active reflects only still-running jobs, total still counts every launched job, and completed entries remain in the registry flagged inactive.

decisions.decision: Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus returns a structured object @{ active; total; activePids } instead of a bare integer.
decisions.rationale: Single-source (B), sound API design (judge 0.81). A structured result is extensible and self-documenting, composes cleanly with the test's peak-sampling (which reads .active), and a meaningful 'total' depends on NOT removing completed entries — reinforcing the atom-05 modification.
alternatives_considered: Return a bare integer active count (rejected: not extensible, hides total/activePids, weaker self-documentation)
decisions.test: Call Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus and assert the result is a PSCustomObject/Hashtable exposing at least an 'active' property (plus 'total' and 'activePids').

decisions.decision: tools/test-readonly-parallel.ps1 launches >=3 'powershell -NoProfile -Command Start-Sleep' jobs (6–8s each), repeatedly samples Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus to PEAK-track the active count, asserts peak >=3, and runs [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile on both lib/parallel.ps1 and itself.
decisions.rationale: Consensus and well-constructed (judge 0.8725). Peak-tracking across repeated samples avoids flakiness from sampling as jobs finish; the 6–8s sleep gives ample headroom for the peak>=3 assert; the ParseFile checks catch parse regressions cheaply and work whether status returns an int or the atom-06 object.
alternatives_considered: Single-shot sampling of the active count (rejected: flaky — a sample can land as jobs are completing and miss the true peak)
decisions.test: Run tools/test-readonly-parallel.ps1: it must pass with peak active >=3 and both files parsing cleanly via Parser::ParseFile (zero errors).

decisions.decision: Make spawning fault-tolerant: wrap each Start-Process in try/catch and record a failed/exited spawn in the registry with proc=$null (inactive) instead of throwing.
decisions.rationale: Single-source (B), clear robustness win (judge 0.8185). One bad job must not abort the whole pool launch; the proc=$null record integrates with the registry and the active-count filter. Some commands spawn then immediately exit (no throw) — the cached-.HasExited liveness check from atom-03 catches that path, so atoms 03 and 08 together are complete.
alternatives_considered: Let Start-Process exceptions propagate (rejected: a single failed spawn aborts the entire pool launch)
decisions.test: Launch an invalid/non-existent command via Start-ReadOnlyAuditJob: it does not throw, the job is recorded inactive (proc=$null), and Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus excludes it from the active count.

rejected.decision: Destructively prune (remove) completed/missing processes from the registry inside Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus (original atom-05).
rejected.why: Mutates state inside a read (Get-) verb, discards the metadata/result-file pointers needed after completion, and breaks both the launched 'total' count (atom-06) and the proc=$null failed-job records (atom-08). Replaced by non-destructive marking, with real cleanup deferred to a separate maintenance function.

rejected.decision: Use a synchronized/thread-safe hashtable for the registry.
rejected.why: Start-Process spawns external OS processes, not in-runspace threads, so there is no concurrent-runspace access to guard. A plain script-scoped hashtable is sufficient and simpler.
Throws when the process has already exited and is vulnerable to PID reuse reporting a dead job as alive. Replaced by reading .HasExited on the cached, session-owned Process handle.

rejected.decision: Place the read-only audit pool in a separate .ps1 file.
rejected.why: It would duplicate Get-ParallelJobsDir; the required isolation from the worktree/merge path is already achieved with a delimited section plus dedicated function prefixes inside lib/parallel.ps1.

open_questions: Scaling the proven mechanism from the demonstration threshold of 3 to the planned concurrency target of 20 (explicitly deferred by the source plan).

Lifecycle of the separate maintenance/cleanup function that atom-05 moved cleanup into: when it runs, and whether it deletes the per-job roaudit_<guid>.{in,out,err,result} temp files in addition to removing stale registry entries.
How downstream audit logic consumes the per-job 'result' file — out of scope for this foundational atom but needed by the next phase.
§14 decisions are 'on the operator' per the source approval_decisions.md — confirm no operator-level decision is still blocking before merge.
implementation_plan: In lib/parallel.ps1, open a clearly delimited block (e.g. '# === Read-Only Audit Pool (BEGIN) ===' / '# === Read-Only Audit Pool (END) ===') separate from all worktree/merge code.
Declare $script:ReadOnlyAuditRegistry as a plain script-scoped hashtable (or list) of root-PID job records.

Implement Start-ReadOnlyAuditJob: allocate roaudit_<guid>.{in,out,err,result} under Get-ParallelJobsDir; call Start-Process -PassThru -NoNewWindow with -RedirectStandardInput/-Output/-Error to the in/out/err files, wrapped in try/catch; on success record jobId, pid, pidTicks, cached Process handle; on failure record the entry with proc=$null.

Implement Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus: iterate the registry, mark entries inactive where the cached handle's .HasExited is true (no removal), and return @{ active; total; activePids } where active = count of entries with a live, non-null handle.
Add a separate maintenance function (out-of-getter) responsible for actually removing stale registry entries and deleting their temp files; do not call it from the getter.

Create tools/test-readonly-parallel.ps1: dot-source lib/parallel.ps1; launch >=3 'powershell -NoProfile -Command Start-Sleep 6..8' jobs via Start-ReadOnlyAuditJob; loop-sample Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus tracking the maximum .active observed; assert peak >=3; run [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile on both lib/parallel.ps1 and the test file and assert zero parse errors; exit non-zero on any failure.
Run the test; confirm it is green with peak active >=3, and confirm grep shows no worktree/merge/cleanup calls from the new section.
Commit both files as a single atomic, atom-sized change (no commit famine).
next_step: Add the delimited Read-Only Audit Pool section to lib/parallel.ps1 — registry + Start-ReadOnlyAuditJob (Start-Process -PassThru, cached handle, four roaudit_<guid> temp files, try/catch→proc=$null) + non-destructive Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus returning @{active;total;activePids} — then create and run tools/test-readonly-parallel.ps1 to prove peak active >=3 and clean ParseFile on both files.

red_team_findings.what: Test bootstrap is under-specified and would make the green-test acceptance fail. implementation_plan step 6 says the test should 'dot-source lib/parallel.ps1' only. But the new code path Start-ReadOnlyAuditJob -> Get-ParallelJobsDir -> Get-BridgeRoot, and Get-BridgeRoot is defined in lib/common.ps1 / lib/features.ps1, NOT in lib/parallel.ps1.
red_team_findings.why: If the test dot-sources only parallel.ps1, the first job launch throws 'Get-BridgeRoot is not recognized'. Because spawning is deliberately fault-tolerant (try/catch -> proc=$null), EVERY job is recorded inactive, peak active = 0, and the peak>=3 assertion fails. The decision must dot-source common.ps1 (or stub Get-BridgeRoot); as written, success_test #1 and #4 (test green) are unmet.

red_team_findings.what: Start-Process -RedirectStandardInput requires the input file to already EXIST on disk; the plan only 'allocates' the roaudit_<guid>.in path without stating it is written first. Every working spawn in this repo creates the input file before launch (deep-audit.ps1:253 WriteAllText $inF, Invoke-CodexParallel parallel.ps1:90), precisely because of this.
red_team_findings.why: If -RedirectStandardInput points at a non-existent .in file, Start-Process throws 'Cannot find path...', the try/catch records proc=$null, and if it hits all jobs the active peak is 0 -> test red. Compounding it: a dummy 'Start-Sleep' job needs no stdin at all, so redirecting stdin is gratuitous added failure surface for the exact assertion being proven.

red_team_findings.what: The atom ships a temp-file leak that reintroduces a previously-fixed regression. Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus is non-destructive by design and 'real cleanup' is deferred to a separate maintenance function that is neither implemented nor called in this atom (open_questions even flags its lifecycle as unknown). So the four roaudit_<guid>.{in,out,err,result} files accumulate in jobs\parallel.
red_team_findings.why: Get-CanaryMetrics/probe machinery (common.ps1:1037-1043) recursively FILE-COUNTS the jobs tree and feeds that count into the adaptive probe timeout. This is the same 'jobs-weighted adaptive probe timeout' inflation that parallel.ps1:720-723 added explicit worker_* reaping to stop. The new pool re-creates that leak (and the 'result' file is never reaped even on the happy path). It passes the atom test but degrades the wider system.

red_team_findings.what: The cached Process handle is never materialized. Every other Start-Process -PassThru site in this codebase immediately does `$null = $proc.Handle` (parallel.ps1:38, 111; 40-agent-invoke.ps1:100,649,805) to retain the OS handle so .HasExited/.Id stay valid after the process exits. The decision relies entirely on .HasExited but never mentions retaining the handle.
red_team_findings.why: Without a retained handle, .HasExited can throw or return stale data after the process exits. If Get-ReadOnlyAuditPoolStatus reads .HasExited per entry without a per-entry try/catch, one exited job makes the whole status call throw, breaking the 'mark inactive' path and the test's repeated sampling. It also silently contradicts the file's own established invariant.

red_team_findings.what: The dummy test cannot prove the contract's actual requirement — 'захват КОРНЕВОГО PID агента' (capture the agent's ROOT PID). Start-Process -PassThru returns the DIRECTLY launched process; for 'powershell -Command Start-Sleep' that is the leaf, so .HasExited is faithful and peak>=3 passes trivially.
red_team_findings.why: Real audit agents are typically launched via a wrapper/launcher that forks the agent and exits (the very reason 'root PID' is emphasized). In that case the captured 'root' handle dies early and .HasExited reports the still-running agent as inactive (false-negative liveness). The success test, built only on direct Start-Sleep processes, structurally cannot detect this, so the 'foundation for parallelism' is unproven for its stated purpose.

red_team_findings.what: pidTicks is justified as a 'PID-reuse anti-reuse stamp', but the design reads liveness exclusively from the cached Process object and never re-resolves a job by PID (Get-Process -Id was explicitly rejected).
red_team_findings.why: Since there is no code path that re-looks-up a process by its PID, there is no path where PID reuse could ever be observed or mis-attributed. The cached-handle design already eliminates that threat, so pidTicks guards nothing — harmless, but the stated rationale is internally inconsistent and adds dead metadata.
